fluff.overview: The CEX-205 Groundhog is a combat engineering exoskeleton produced by Blue Shot Weapons on Solaris VII. Introduced in 3062, the Groundhog was designed as a field-ready engineering platform capable of supporting military and mercenary operations through a modular manipulator system that allows rapid reconfiguration for different tasks. The suit's interchangeable tool mounts accept a wide range of equipment, from armored gloves suitable for light combat duties to specialized industrial tools for heavy labor, mine clearance, and salvage work. An integrated searchlight and onboard mission equipment storage further extend the Groundhog's operational utility. Heavily armored for an exoskeleton, the Groundhog earned a reputation as one of the first truly battlefield-ready engineering exoskeletons available on the open market.
fluff.capabilities:
The Armored Glove configuration equips the CEX-205 with reinforced gauntlets on both manipulator mounts, giving operators the ability to handle standard infantry weapons and conduct anti-BattleMech swarm and leg attacks. At four hundred kilograms, the Groundhog is a maximum-weight exoskeleton protected by one hundred kilograms of standard armor, enough to resist small arms fire but offering little protection against heavier ordnance. The suit's ground speed of thirty kilometers per hour keeps pace with foot infantry, though the lack of jump capability limits vertical mobility in urban or broken terrain.

An integral searchlight supports low-visibility operations, while the body-mounted mission equipment storage bay provides one hundred forty-five kilograms of carrying capacity. Of the Groundhog's available configurations, the Armored Glove loadout is the most combat-oriented, though operators should not mistake the suit's ability to engage BattleMechs for genuine offensive power. The Groundhog remains an engineering platform pressed into a combat-adjacent role, not a dedicated fighting suit.
fluff.deployment: Clan formations that acquired Groundhog exoskeletons through salvage or trade organized operators into five-trooper Points, consistent with standard Clan military structure. The Armored Glove configuration saw limited Clan adoption given the generally low regard for industrial exoskeletons among warrior caste personnel, but labor and garrison castes occasionally fielded Points for facility defense and engineering support where dedicated Elemental suits were unavailable or unwarranted.
fluff.history:
Blue Shot Weapons had long served a niche market on Solaris VII, producing industrial exo-suits primarily sold to arena management companies for routine maintenance and emergency MechWarrior extractions. The CEX-205 Groundhog, introduced in 3062, marked a deliberate shift in the company's ambitions. Drawing on advances in Inner Sphere battle armor technology, Blue Shot designed the Groundhog as their first truly field-ready combat engineering exoskeleton, offering military and mercenary units a rugged, modular platform far beyond their earlier commercial-grade offerings.

Blue Shot marketed the full line of manipulator configurations in paired sets, emphasizing the suit's adaptability for diverse field operations. Arena operators on Solaris VII also adopted the Groundhog for "tunnel rat" operations during the FedCom Civil War, using the suit's improved communications equipment and searchlight for underground engagements.

The Word of Blake invasion of Solaris VII in 3068 dealt a severe blow to Blue Shot Weapons. The company's production facilities suffered catastrophic damage during the fighting, with capacity reportedly falling below ten percent. By 3071, the damage proved insurmountable, and the Groundhog was officially discontinued. Persistent rumors of a jump-capable variant designated the CEX-250 Leapfrog had circulated for some time, but with the Blue Shot plant in ruins, the design never reached production.
